subject: Technical deep dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs & deployment topology
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@acme.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego@acme.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 14:15:00 -0700
Subject: Technical deep dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs & deployment topology

Hi Samantha / Diego —

Thanks again for taking the time today for the technical deep dive. Below is a concise recap of the pain points you shared, the goals we discussed, and the next steps we agreed on. Please flag anything I missed or that needs correction.

Pain points / constraints (Acme):
- Peak search/query volume: ~25k QPS during peak windows, 6k steady-state.
- P99 latency requirement: <= 120ms for short-form generation and reranking flows.
- Throughput requirement: sustain bursts to 25k QPS with <2x latency degradation; average token length ~12.
- Data residency: production inference must run in us-west-2 (VPC/private) for compliance.
- Model family preference: open LLaMA-family variants, but willing to evaluate Redwood-verified quantized variants if quality meets baseline.

Architecture notes we discussed:
- Primary topology: Dedicated pool (reserved GPUs) in us-west-2 for production serving; fallback to hosted low-cost pool for non-sensitive workloads.
- Split traffic by route: short prompts -> optimized tnt-quant (4-bit) variant; long-context ranking -> fp16 on larger instance with KV cache pinned.
- Autoscaling: target CPU/GPU utilization-based autoscale with burst capacity for scheduled marketing events; request-level routing to avoid cold starts.
- Caching: prefix/KV cache for repeated prompts; plan to enable prefix cache for 70% of high-frequency queries.

SLOs and measurements:
- Latency SLOs: P50 25-40ms, P95 70-90ms, P99 <=120ms for short-form generation (1-2 tokens).
- Throughput SLOs: sustain 6k QPS steady with headroom to 25k QPS bursts via reserved capacity + burst pool.
- Observability: per-route token-level latency + cost breakdown, traceable to model variant and instance type.

Open questions / items to validate (action owners):
- Model accuracy baseline: Acme to share 1k representative prompts + evaluation metric (Diego)  — owner: Acme (Diego).
- Quantized quality check: Redwood to run A/B on tnt-quant vs fp16 for 1k eval set  — owner: Marissa / Research.
- Network egress and VPC peering: confirm VPC peering options and egress costs for us-west-2  — owner: Ethan.
- Contract/SLA ramp: confirm preferred contract term and committed QPS for Dedicated  — owner: Marissa / Sales.

Attachments included:
- redwood-deployment-diagram.png (deployment topology + routing policy)
- slo-summary.pdf (SLO table + measurement plan)

Next steps (timeline):
1) Acme: share eval prompts and expected accuracy thresholds by Mon 3/29. (Diego)
2) Redwood: run quantized vs fp16 eval and provide quality/latency report by Fri 4/2. (Marissa / Research)
3) Infrastructure check: Redwood infra team to confirm VPC peering and egress options by Wed 3/31. (Ethan)
4) Follow-up call to review results and discuss Dedicated sizing: propose Wed 4/6 or Thu 4/7.

Thanks  — happy to jump on a quick call if that's easier.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Quick follow-ups from infra side — thanks for the great session earlier. A couple of clarifications so we can size the Dedicated pool and run accurate perf tests: 

1) Burst profile: can you confirm expected burst duration? Is 10-15 minutes typical for marketing pushes or do you see multi-hour sustained peaks?
2) Tokenization: are your prompts mostly English short queries (avg 12 tokens) or do you have multi-turn contexts we should account for?
3) Security: will Acme require HSM/KMS integration for model keys or only for data at rest?

If you prefer, we can capture this in a short form — happy to send a 3-question survey.

Thanks Marissa — this looks good and accurately reflects what we discussed. Quick answers inline: 

1) Burst duration: typically 8-20 minutes for marketing pushes; we see a <30-minute tail as traffic decays. Occasionally (quarterly) we have hour-long spikes for major product drops.
2) Tokenization: majority are short English queries ~10-14 tokens; separate longer contextual sessions exist for advanced users (approx 5% of traffic).
3) KMS/HSM: we will require KMS for data at rest initially; HSM for key custody may be requested after initial rollout (TBD).
